verdicts.argument: Both lenses kill it. I re-checked the FY2024 10-K (index p.20): the 'could also affect the Medicaid rebate obligations and the ceiling prices charged to covered entities under Section 340B' sentence is there, as both of us found in round 1. The obviousness skeptic adds that the same sentence ran in the 10-Qs from 2024Q3 and that 340B mix came up on calls. On my lens, the 62.7% share mixes years and mixes gross with net. With no 'new' disclosure left to stand on, severity goes up to fatal.
verdicts.correction: At most a language-drift footnote: the 340B wording hardened to 'pervasive violations'. No number.

round2.conceded: Obviousness is right that the spillover was already in the FY2024 10-K and the 10-Qs. I raise the severity from major to fatal.
round2.held: My math objection stands on its own: 7,187/11,467 adds 2025 Part D gross spend to 2024 Medicaid reimbursed amounts and divides by net sales.
round2.narrowed: Only the 340B wording drift is left, and it is unquantified.

verdicts.argument: We agree. Long-acting HIV was already priority (ii) in FY2024 (10-K FY2024 index p.38), and this is the starter thread. On my lens there is no supportable number: the $2,075M is an arbitrary 10% illustration, and the HIV total includes Gilead's own long-acting products.
verdicts.correction: Supporting footnote only: the nucleoside-preference risk sentence was dropped after FY2024 and the 2025Q1 10-Q.

round2.conceded: Obviousness adds the starter-thread framing and the proxy pp.2 and 31 priority printing. I accept both and raise the severity to fatal.

verdicts.argument: I verified the obviousness skeptic's sources. The 2025Q4 earnings slides p.25 say 'Excluding an estimated $1.1 billion in Part D Redesign headwinds, total product sales +5%'. The 2024Q4 call p.10 (grade C, CFO Andrew Dickinson) says 'approximately $1.1 billion, including $900 million in HIV'. Measured against the company-wide figure, the reader's residual is 1,227 - 1,100 = about $127M, or 0.4% of revenue. That is below the materiality threshold even before my round 1 objection. That objection still applies: the rate-at-2024 counterfactual counts list-price inflation that was never net revenue (Biktarvy WAC +5.9% against gross +5.35%), plus mix (Veklury -$888M), so the true unexplained amount is plausibly about zero. The 250 bps headline is printed in the 10-K's own GTN table, and the dollar rebate split is still disclosed.
verdicts.correction: Usable only as context: GTN +250 bps, about 90% of it the $1.1B Part D headwind management sized. No finding.

round2.conceded: In round 1 I held c03 in narrowed form. I now concede it. Management gave a company-wide $1.1B figure that I did not find, which shrinks the residual to an immaterial $127M, and the 250 bps rate rise is printed in the 10-K itself.
round2.held: The '$1.2B lost net revenue' framing is wrong arithmetic regardless of which Part D figure is used, because list inflation and mix both inflate the counterfactual.
round2.narrowed: From 'held, narrowed' to refuted: nothing material and unsaid remains.

verdicts.argument: This is the only GILD candidate that is both material in size and unsaid. On my math, the pre-commercial Trodelvy balance was $613M (10-K FY2025 index p.80), then $638M (10-Q 2026Q1 index p.18, which I verified), then $568M (10-Q 2026Q2 index p.21). A full write-down of $568M equals 4.3% of FY2025 non-GAAP operating income ($13,193M), about 1.9% of revenue, and about $0.36 per share pretax-to-EPS. That uses the proxy's own scaling of $0.25 per $400M (proxy index p.116), so it is about 4.4% of FY2025 non-GAAP EPS of $8.15. That clears the materiality bar. It is a contingent, one-time charge, not a recurring earnings effect: it occurs only if FDA does not approve the new process, and Gilead might exclude it from non-GAAP. The broader inventory and receivables build ($779M inventory, $493M receivables) is acknowledged in MD&A (index p.46), so on obviousness only the Trodelvy line is unsaid. Agree with obviousness that the ASCENT-07 link is irrelevant.
verdicts.correction: Finding, framed narrowly: '$568M (peak $638M in Q1 2026) of Trodelvy inventory sits on a manufacturing process FDA has not approved. That is about 41% of a year of Trodelvy sales, and a write-off would be about $0.36 per share, or 4% of non-GAAP operating income, one time. It is disclosed only in the inventory footnote and never on a call or in a release.' Size it as a contingent one-time risk, not an earnings trend.

round2.conceded: The ASCENT-07 tie-in should go, as both of us said. The MD&A already states the general inventory build, so only the Trodelvy line is non-obvious.
round2.held: It is material: about $0.36 per share and 4% of operating income in a write-down case, which is well above 'a few cents of EPS'.
round2.narrowed: Drop the 21.7% inventory and DIO framing, which is acknowledged in the MD&A and uses GAAP COGS that includes amortization. Keep only the Trodelvy pre-commercial balance, as a contingent one-time risk, and add the $638M Q1 2026 peak.

verdicts.argument: I verified the grade-A 2025Q3 call p.9. CFO Andrew Dickinson says it 'relates to an IP asset sale from 2018' and 'Excluding the $400 million non-recurring other revenue, non-GAAP diluted EPS would have been $2.22'. The 2026Q2 call p.1 (grade C) calls the $156M 'a nonrecurring and noncash item'. The candidate's premise that the ex-item figure is not given to investors is false: management handed investors the exact ex-item EPS. My round 1 math ($0.25, 3.1% of FY2025 non-GAAP EPS) is still correct, but a correct number that management already stated is not a finding.
verdicts.correction: Residue only: 'not expected to reoccur' was followed by a second $156M true-up, about $0.10 and under 1% of revenue. That is also flagged by management, so it is not a finding.

round2.conceded: In round 1 this was my cleanest survivor. I concede it. My round 1 note that the release named it as an EPS driver should have led me to the call, where the CFO gives the ex-item EPS of $2.22.
round2.held: The arithmetic ($0.25 per $400M, 3.1% of EPS) is right. It is just already said.

verdicts.argument: We agree on refutation for different reasons. Mine: it compares a 2025 statement with 2026 drivers, and the 'half' split has no source. Theirs: the reordered drivers are on Gilead's own Q2 2026 slide p.9 and in the 8-K, and an analyst asked about volume versus mix. I verified slide p.9 in round 1.

round2.conceded: The price-led drivers were said plainly on the slide and in the release, so I raise the severity to fatal.
round2.held: Even if it were unsaid, the impact (about $91M a quarter, assumed) is an invented split.

verdicts.argument: We agree. On my lens it is immaterial: Gilead's own -0.7% ASP drift on an $800M guide is about $6M, and the reader's $35M is 0.12% of revenue, mostly ViiV's price rise. The obviousness skeptic adds that twice-yearly dosing is the approval press-release headline.

round2.conceded: The obviousness kill on the dosing headline is right, so I raise the severity to fatal.

verdicts.argument: I verified label v19 p.1: treatment-experienced use is limited to virologically suppressed patients. v22 p.1 adds 'with an antiretroviral treatment history and not virologically suppressed'. The widening is real and, per obviousness, unannounced. On materiality it is not a finding. At $29.9M net per 1,000 patients (my round 1 check), reaching 1% of revenue (about $294M) needs about 10,000 incremental patients who would not otherwise be on Biktarvy. Nothing in the index sizes the resistance-free, viremic, treatment-experienced pool. The 365k non-suppressed figure (1,044,000 x 35%) mixes in untreated and undiagnosed-care people, and many of the target patients were likely already on Biktarvy off-label. Unsaid but not shown to be material.
verdicts.correction: Use it as the lead fine-print point in the product comparison (share defense ahead of the 2028 MFP), not as a sized finding.

round2.conceded: Obviousness is right that it is unsaid. The v19 to v22 diff confirms a genuine widening.
round2.held: It is refuted as a material finding: there is no sourced pool size, and the materiality threshold needs about 10,000 incremental patients.
round2.narrowed: Not material as sized, but valid for the product section.

verdicts.argument: I verified the White House fact sheet p.1: 'The agreements require the nine companies to repatriate increased foreign revenue'. Merck's 10-K FY2025 (index p.54) says Merck 'agreed to repatriate and share with the Federal government a portion of foreign revenue'. My round 1 search wording missed Merck's 'repatriate' phrasing, so I wrongly said no peer discloses the term. The uniqueness leg is false. My other objections stand: AbbVie is 22.5% not 16.9%, Merck's Keytruda is expected at 48.7%, and every company has the same tariff date.
verdicts.correction: Context row only: Biktarvy 48.7% of revenue in IRA selection.

round2.conceded: My round 1 correction claimed Gilead was the only company to disclose the repatriation term. That was wrong: Merck discloses it, and the term is standard across the nine deals. I raise the severity to fatal.
round2.held: The peer-number errors (AbbVie, Merck's Keytruda) and the identical tariff pause dates stand.
round2.narrowed: Drop my 'only shortlist company to disclose' wording entirely.

verdicts.argument: Biktarvy is the material product ($14,334M, 48.7% of revenue). The v19 to v22 indication widening is the one fine-print point that is both verified and unsaid, but it is unsized (see c08).
verdicts.correction: Lead the product section with the v19 to v22 change, framed as share defense. Use no revenue number.

round2.conceded: Agree with obviousness that the HBV and pediatric contrasts are filler.
round2.held: The product pick is right on size.
round2.narrowed: Fine-print edge = the v22 widening only.

overall: After both rounds, GILD has one candidate that is material and unsaid: the footnote-only $568M (peak $638M) of Trodelvy inventory on a process FDA has not approved. A write-down would be about $0.36 per share, or 4% of non-GAAP operating income, one time and contingent. The Biktarvy v22 label widening is unsaid but unsized, and everything else is either already stated by management (c03's $1.1B, c05's $2.22 ex-item EPS, c06's slide) or immaterial.
